name: NC Math 2017
source: North Carolina Standard Course of Study
description: North Carolina's K-12 mathematics standards as taught through 2027-28: kindergarten to grade 8 (adopted June 2017), NC Math 1 to 4 and Precalculus. One topic per numbered standard, grouped by domain.

topics.name: Count to 100
topics.description: Say the counting sequence to 100 by ones and by tens, noticing its patterns.
topics.statement:
Know number names and recognize patterns in the counting sequence by:
- Counting to 100 by ones.
- Counting to 100 by tens.

topics.name: Count on from any number
topics.description: Continue counting forward from a given number instead of starting again at 1.
topics.statement: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence, instead of having to begin at 1.

topics.name: Write numbers 0 to 20
topics.description: Write the numerals 0 to 20 and use them to record how many objects there are, with 0 meaning none.
topics.statement: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20, with 0 representing a count of no objects.

topics.name: Numbers and quantities
topics.description: Connect counting to quantity through one-to-one correspondence, cardinality and recognising up to 5 objects at a glance.
topics.statement:
Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities.
- When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object (one-to-one correspondence).
- Recognize that the last number named tells the number of objects counted regardless of their arrangement (cardinality).
- State the number of objects in a group, of up to 5 objects, without counting the objects (perceptual subitizing).

topics.name: Count to answer how many
topics.description: Count out up to 20 objects, name the number one more, and count objects in lines, arrays, circles and scattered groups.
topics.statement:
Count to answer “How many?” in the following situations.
- Given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.
- Given up to 20 objects, name the next successive number when an object is added, recognizing the quantity is one more/greater.
- Given 20 objects arranged in a line, a rectangular array, and a circle, identify how many.
- Given 10 objects in a scattered arrangement, identify how many.

topics.name: Compare groups of objects
topics.description: Tell whether one group of up to 10 objects has more, fewer or the same number as another by matching or counting.
topics.statement: Identify whether the number of objects, within 10, in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, by using matching and counting strategies.

topics.name: Compare numbers to 10
topics.description: Compare two written numerals between 1 and 10.
topics.statement: Compare two numbers, within 10, presented as written numerals.

topics.name: Show addition and subtraction
topics.description: Represent addition and subtraction within 10 with objects, fingers, drawings, actions, words or expressions, and connect the representations.
topics.statement:
Represent addition and subtraction, within 10:
- Use a variety of representations such as objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or expressions.
- Demonstrate understanding of addition and subtraction by making connections among representations.

topics.name: Word problems within 10
topics.description: Solve add-to, take-from and put-together/take-apart word problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
topics.statement:
Solve addition and subtraction word problems, within 10, using objects or drawings to represent the problem, when solving:
- Add to/Take From-Result Unknown
- Put Together/ Take Apart (Total Unknown and Two Addends Unknown)

topics.name: Break apart numbers to 10
topics.description: Split numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way and record each split with a drawing or expression.
topics.statement: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or expression.

topics.name: Make ten
topics.description: Find the number that makes 10 with any number from 0 to 10, using objects or drawings, and record it.
topics.statement: For any number from 0 to 10, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or expression.

topics.name: See small groups combined
topics.description: Recognise and combine small groups with totals up to 5 without counting one by one.
topics.statement: Recognize and combine groups with totals up to 5 (conceptual subitizing).

topics.name: Add and subtract within 5
topics.description: Add and subtract within 5 quickly and accurately.
topics.statement: Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction within 5.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Teen numbers as ten and ones
topics.description: Build and break apart the numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones, and record them.
topics.statement:
Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones by:
- Using objects or drawings.
- Recording each composition or decomposition by a drawing or expression.
- Understanding that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

topics.name: Measurable attributes
topics.description: Describe the measurable attributes of objects, including several attributes of one object.
topics.statement: Describe measurable attributes of objects; and describe several different measurable attributes of a single object.

topics.name: Compare two objects directly
topics.description: Compare two objects by a shared attribute to see which has more or less of it, and describe the difference.
topics.statement: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference.

topics.name: Sort and count by category
topics.description: Sort objects into categories, count each category and order the categories by count.
topics.statement: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.

topics.name: Shapes and positions
topics.description: Name shapes seen in the environment and describe where objects are using position words.
topics.statement: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of objects using positional terms.

topics.name: Name shapes
topics.description: Name common flat and solid shapes correctly whatever their size or orientation.
topics.statement: Correctly name squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres regardless of their orientations or overall size.

topics.name: Flat and solid shapes
topics.description: Identify common shapes as two-dimensional or three-dimensional.
topics.statement: Identify squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres as two-dimensional or three-dimensional.

topics.name: Compare shapes
topics.description: Compare flat and solid shapes of different sizes and orientations, describing likenesses, differences and attributes in everyday language.
topics.statement: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, attributes and other properties.

topics.name: Build and draw shapes
topics.description: Model shapes from the world by building and drawing flat shapes and building solid ones.
topics.statement:
Model shapes in the world by:
- Building and drawing triangles, rectangles, squares, hexagons, circles.
- Building cubes, cones, spheres, and cylinders.

topics.name: Compose larger shapes
topics.description: Put simple shapes together to make larger shapes.
topics.statement: Compose larger shapes from simple shapes.

topics.name: Word problems within 20
topics.description: Represent and solve addition and subtraction word problems within 20 with unknowns in different positions, using objects, drawings and equations.
topics.statement:
Represent and solve addition and subtraction word problems, within 20, with unknowns, by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, when solving:
- Add to/Take from-Change Unknown
- Put together/Take Apart-Addend Unknown
- Compare-Difference Unknown

topics.name: Add three numbers in problems
topics.description: Represent and solve word problems adding three whole numbers with a sum up to 20.
topics.statement: Represent and solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number.

topics.name: Properties of addition
topics.description: Use the commutative and associative properties as strategies when adding.
topics.statement: Apply the commutative and associative properties as strategies for solving addition problems.

topics.name: Unknown addend problems
topics.description: Solve missing-addend problems within 20 by adding on or by turning them into subtraction.
topics.statement: Solve an unknown-addend problem, within 20, by using addition strategies and/or changing it to a subtraction problem.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 10
topics.description: Add and subtract within 10 fluently.
topics.statement: Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction within 10.

topics.name: Strategies within 20
topics.description: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as counting on, making ten, number lines and related facts.
topics.statement:
Add and subtract, within 20, using strategies such as:
- Counting on
- Making ten
- Decomposing a number leading to a ten
- Using the relationship between addition and subtraction
- Using a number line
- Creating equivalent but simpler or known sums

topics.name: Meaning of the equal sign
topics.description: Use the meaning of the equal sign to decide whether addition and subtraction equations are true.
topics.statement: Apply understanding of the equal sign to determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true.

topics.name: Find the unknown number
topics.description: Find the missing whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three numbers.
topics.statement: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation involving three whole numbers.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Count to 150
topics.description: Count up to 150 starting from any number below 150.
topics.statement: Count to 150, starting at any number less than 150.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Read and write numbers to 100
topics.description: Read and write numerals to 100 and use them to record a number of objects.
topics.statement: Read and write numerals, and represent a number of objects with a written numeral, to 100.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Tens and ones
topics.description: Understand a two-digit number as tens and ones, including making a ten from ten ones and the decade numbers.
topics.statement:
Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones.
- Unitize by making a ten from a collection of ten ones.
- Model the numbers from 11 to 19 as composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
- Demonstrate that the numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens, with 0 ones.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Compare two-digit numbers
topics.description: Compare two-digit numbers by their tens and ones and record the result with >, = or <.
topics.statement: Compare two two-digit numbers based on the value of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Add within 100
topics.description: Add a one-digit number or a multiple of 10 to a two-digit number using models and place-value strategies, explaining the reasoning.
topics.statement:
Using concrete models or drawings, strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and explaining the reasoning used, add, within 100, in the following situations:
- A two-digit number and a one-digit number
- A two-digit number and a multiple of 10

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Ten more and ten less
topics.description: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number and explain how.
topics.statement: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Subtract multiples of 10
topics.description: Subtract multiples of 10 from 10 to 90 using models, number lines and place-value strategies, explaining the reasoning.
topics.statement:
Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90, explaining the reasoning, using:
- Concrete models and drawings
- Number lines
- Strategies based on place value
- Properties of operations
- The relationship between addition and subtraction

topics.name: Order and compare lengths
topics.description: Order three objects by length and compare two lengths indirectly using a third object.
topics.statement: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

topics.name: Measure with non-standard units
topics.description: Measure length by laying copies of a shorter unit end to end and state it as a whole number of units.
topics.statement:
Measure lengths with non-standard units.
- Express the length of an object as a whole number of non-standard length units.
- Measure by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end (iterating) with no gaps or overlaps.

topics.name: Time to the half hour
topics.description: Tell and write time in hours and half hours on analog and digital clocks.
topics.statement: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

topics.name: Coins and their values
topics.description: Identify quarters, dimes and nickels and relate their values to pennies.
topics.statement: Identify quarters, dimes, and nickels and relate their values to pennies.

topics.name: Data with three categories
topics.description: Organise, show and answer questions about data in up to three categories.
topics.statement:
Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories.
- Ask and answer questions about the total number of data points.
- Ask and answer questions about how many in each category.
- Ask and answer questions about how many more or less are in one category than in another.

topics.name: Attributes of shapes
topics.description: Tell defining from non-defining attributes and build and draw flat and solid shapes with given attributes.
topics.statement:
Distinguish between defining and non-defining attributes and create shapes with defining attributes by:
- Building and drawing triangles, rectangles, squares, trapezoids, hexagons, circles.
- Building cubes, rectangular prisms, cones, spheres, and cylinders.

topics.name: Composite shapes
topics.description: Make flat and solid composite shapes from simpler shapes and name their parts.
topics.statement:
Create composite shapes by:
- Making a two-dimensional composite shape using rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, and half-circles naming the components of the new shape.
- Making a three-dimensional composite shape using cubes, rectangular prisms, cones, and cylinders, naming the components of the new shape.

topics.name: Halves and fourths
topics.description: Split circles and rectangles into two or four equal shares, name them as halves and fourths, and see that more shares are smaller.
topics.statement:
Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares.
- Describe the shares as halves and fourths, as half of and fourth of.
- Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares.
- Explain that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

topics.name: Word problems within 100
topics.description: Represent and solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100 with unknowns in all positions.
topics.statement:
Represent and solve addition and subtraction word problems, within 100, with unknowns in all positions, by using representations and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, when solving:
- One-Step problems:
- Add to/Take from-Start Unknown
- Compare-Bigger Unknown
- Compare-Smaller Unknown
- Two-Step problems involving single digits
- Add to/Take from- Change Unknown
- Add to/Take From- Result Unknown

topics.name: Mental math within 20
topics.description: Add and subtract within 20 fluently using mental strategies.
topics.statement: Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction, within 20, using mental strategies.

topics.name: Odd and even numbers
topics.description: Decide whether a group of up to 20 objects is odd or even by pairing, splitting into two equal groups, or writing a doubles equation.
topics.statement:
Determine whether a group of objects, within 20, has an odd or even number of members by:
- Pairing objects, then counting them by 2s.
- Determining whether objects can be placed into two equal groups.
- Writing an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

topics.name: Arrays and repeated addition
topics.description: Use addition to total objects in arrays of up to 5 by 5 and write the total as a sum of equal addends.
topics.statement: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Hundreds, tens and ones
topics.description: Understand a three-digit number as hundreds, tens and ones, including making a hundred from ten tens and regrouping.
topics.statement:
Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones.
- Unitize by making a hundred from a collection of ten tens.
- Demonstrate that the numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds, with 0 tens and 0 ones.
- Compose and decompose numbers using various groupings of hundreds, tens, and ones.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Count and skip-count to 1000
topics.description: Count within 1000 and skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s.
topics.statement: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Read and write numbers to 1000
topics.description: Read and write numbers within 1000 as numerals, in words and in expanded form.
topics.statement: Read and write numbers, within 1000, using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Compare three-digit numbers
topics.description: Compare three-digit numbers by their hundreds, tens and ones and record with >, = or <.
topics.statement: Compare two three-digit numbers based on the value of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Add and subtract within 100
topics.description: Add and subtract within 100 fluently, choosing and comparing place-value and property-based strategies.
topics.statement:
Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction, within 100, by:
- Flexibly using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
- Comparing addition and subtraction strategies, and explaining why they work.
- Selecting an appropriate strategy in order to efficiently compute sums and differences.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Add up to three numbers
topics.description: Add up to three two-digit numbers using place value and properties of operations.
topics.statement: Add up to three two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Add and subtract within 1000
topics.description: Add and subtract within 1000 with models and place-value strategies, linking each strategy to a written method.
topics.statement:
Add and subtract, within 1000, relating the strategy to a written method, using:
- Concrete models or drawings
- Strategies based on place value
- Properties of operations
- Relationship between addition and subtraction

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Add or subtract 10 and 100
topics.description: Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from numbers between 100 and 900.
topics.statement: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900.

topics.name: Measure with standard tools
topics.description: Measure lengths in standard units choosing tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks and tape measures.
topics.statement: Measure the length of an object in standard units by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

topics.name: Measure with two units
topics.description: Measure one object in two different units and explain how the measurements relate to the unit size.
topics.statement: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

topics.name: Estimate lengths
topics.description: Estimate lengths in inches, feet, yards, centimeters and meters.
topics.statement: Estimate lengths in using standard units of inches, feet, yards, centimeters, and meters.

topics.name: Compare lengths
topics.description: Measure how much longer one object is than another in a standard unit.
topics.statement: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

topics.name: Length word problems
topics.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems about lengths within 100, using equations with an unknown.
topics.statement: Use addition and subtraction, within 100, to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, using equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

topics.name: Number line diagrams
topics.description: Show whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line and show sums and differences within 100 on it.
topics.statement: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points and represent whole-number sums and differences, within 100, on a number line.

topics.name: Time to five minutes
topics.description: Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks, using a.m. and p.m.
topics.statement: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

topics.name: Money word problems
topics.description: Solve word problems with coins up to 99 cents and with whole dollars, using the cent and dollar symbols.
topics.statement:
Solve word problems involving:
- Quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies within 99¢, using ¢ symbols appropriately.
- Whole dollar amounts, using the $ symbol appropriately.

topics.name: Picture and bar graphs
topics.description: Organise data in up to four categories in picture and bar graphs and solve simple problems from them.
topics.statement:
Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to four categories.
- Draw a picture graph and a bar graph with a single-unit scale to represent a data set.
- Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a picture and a bar graph.

topics.name: Polygons and solids
topics.description: Recognise and draw triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons and hexagons with given attributes, and describe rectangular prisms and cubes.
topics.statement: Recognize and draw triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons, having specified attributes; recognize and describe attributes of rectangular prisms and cubes.

topics.name: Halves, thirds and fourths
topics.description: Split circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal shares, name them, and see that equal shares can differ in shape.
topics.statement:
Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares.
- Describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, fourths, fourth of, quarter of.
- Describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths.
- Explain that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

topics.name: Meaning of multiplication
topics.description: Interpret products of factors up to 10 as equal groups and explain strategies such as arrays, repeated addition and the properties.
topics.statement:
For products of whole numbers with two factors up to and including 10:
- Interpret the factors as representing the number of equal groups and the number of objects in each group.
- Illustrate and explain strategies including arrays, repeated addition, decomposing a factor, and applying the commutative and associative properties.

topics.name: Meaning of division
topics.description: Interpret one-digit quotients as group counts or group sizes and explain strategies such as arrays and repeated subtraction.
topics.statement:
For whole-number quotients of whole numbers with a one-digit divisor and a one-digit quotient:
- Interpret the divisor and quotient in a division equation as representing the number of equal groups and the number of objects in each group.
- Illustrate and explain strategies including arrays, repeated addition or subtraction, and decomposing a factor.

topics.name: Multiplication and division problems
topics.description: Represent and solve one-step multiplication and division word problems with factors and divisors up to 10.
topics.statement:
Represent, interpret, and solve one-step problems involving multiplication and division.
- Solve multiplication word problems with factors up to and including 10. Represent the problem using arrays, pictures, and/or equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
- Solve division word problems with a divisor and quotient up to and including 10. Represent the problem using arrays, pictures, repeated subtraction and/or equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

topics.name: Unknown factor problems
topics.description: Solve unknown-factor problems with division strategies or by turning them into multiplication.
topics.statement: Solve an unknown-factor problem, by using division strategies and/or changing it to a multiplication problem.

topics.name: Multiply and divide within 100
topics.description: Multiply and divide fluently with factors up to 10, knowing the products from memory and using the link between the operations.
topics.statement:
Demonstrate fluency with multiplication and division with factors, quotients and divisors up to and including 10.
- Know from memory all products with factors up to and including 10.
- Illustrate and explain using the relationship between multiplication and division.
- Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

topics.name: Two-step word problems
topics.description: Solve two-step word problems with addition, subtraction and multiplication, writing equations with an unknown.
topics.statement: Solve two-step word problems using addition, subtraction, and multiplication, representing problems using equations with a symbol for the unknown number.

topics.name: Multiplication patterns
topics.description: Find and explain patterns on a hundreds board or a multiplication table.
topics.statement: Interpret patterns of multiplication on a hundreds board and/or multiplication table.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Add and subtract to 1,000
topics.description: Add and subtract whole numbers up to 1,000, estimating to check answers and using expanded form and inverse operations.
topics.statement:
Add and subtract whole numbers up to and including 1,000.
- Use estimation strategies to assess reasonableness of answers.
- Model and explain how the relationship between addition and subtraction can be applied to solve addition and subtraction problems.
- Use expanded form to decompose numbers and then find sums and differences.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Multiply by multiples of 10
topics.description: Multiply a one-digit number by a multiple of 10 from 10 to 90 using models based on place value and properties.
topics.statement: Use concrete and pictorial models, based on place value and the properties of operations, to find the product of a one-digit whole number by a multiple of 10 in the range 10–90.

topics.name: Unit fractions
topics.description: Understand a unit fraction with denominator 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8 as one equal part of a whole, using area and length models.

topics.name: Fractions on models
topics.description: Interpret fractions as counts of unit fractions using area models and the number line.
topics.statement:
Interpret fractions with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 using area and length models.
- Using an area model, explain that the numerator of a fraction represents the number of equal parts of the unit fraction.
- Using a number line, explain that the numerator of a fraction represents the number of lengths of the unit fraction from 0.

topics.name: Equivalent fractions
topics.description: Show equivalent fractions with area and length models, including fractions equal to one and to whole numbers.
topics.statement:
Represent equivalent fractions with area and length models by:
- Composing and decomposing fractions into equivalent fractions using related fractions: halves, fourths and eighths; thirds and sixths.
- Explaining that a fraction with the same numerator and denominator equals one whole.
- Expressing whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

topics.name: Compare fractions
topics.description: Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator by reasoning about size, recording with >, < or =, for the same whole.
topics.statement: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size, using area and length models, and using the >, <, and = symbols. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole with denominators: halves, fourths and eighths; thirds and sixths.

topics.name: Time to the minute
topics.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and solve problems about elapsed time within one hour.
topics.statement: Tell and write time to the nearest minute. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals within the same hour.

topics.name: Customary measurement
topics.description: Estimate and measure length, capacity and weight in customary units and solve one-step problems with them.
topics.statement:
Solve problems involving customary measurement.
- Estimate and measure lengths in customary units to the quarter-inch and half-inch, and feet and yards to the whole unit.
- Estimate and measure capacity and weight in customary units to a whole number: cups, pints, quarts, gallons, ounces, and pounds.
- Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving whole number measurements of length, weight, and capacity in the same customary units.

topics.name: Scaled picture and bar graphs
topics.description: Collect data, show it in frequency tables and scaled graphs, and answer how-many-more and how-many-less questions.
topics.statement:
Represent and interpret scaled picture and bar graphs:
- Collect data by asking a question that yields data in up to four categories.
- Make a representation of data and interpret data in a frequency table, scaled picture graph, and/or scaled bar graph with axes provided.
- Solve one and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information from these graphs

topics.name: Area by tiling
topics.description: Find the area of a rectangle by covering it with unit squares and counting them.
topics.statement: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling without gaps or overlaps and counting unit squares.

topics.name: Area and multiplication
topics.description: Relate area to multiplication and addition, including splitting a rectangle into two smaller ones.
topics.statement:
Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.
- Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
- Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.
- Use tiles and/or arrays to illustrate and explain that the area of a rectangle can be found by partitioning it into two smaller rectangles, and that the area of the large rectangle is the sum of the two smaller rectangles.

topics.name: Perimeter of polygons
topics.description: Find the perimeter of a polygon from its sides and find an unknown side from the perimeter.
topics.statement: Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, and finding an unknown side length.

topics.name: Compose and classify quadrilaterals
topics.description: Reason about composing and decomposing triangles and quadrilaterals and draw examples of each type of quadrilateral.
topics.statement:
Reason with two-dimensional shapes and their attributes.
- Investigate, describe, and reason about composing triangles and quadrilaterals and decomposing quadrilaterals.
- Recognize and draw examples and non-examples of types of quadrilaterals including rhombuses, rectangles, squares, parallelograms, and trapezoids.

topics.name: Multiplicative comparison
topics.description: Interpret multiplication as comparison and solve such word problems, telling them apart from additive comparisons.
topics.statement: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison. Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparisons using models and equations with a symbol for the unknown number. Distinguish multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

topics.name: Multi-step word problems
topics.description: Solve two-step whole-number word problems with all four operations, interpreting remainders and checking by estimation.
topics.statement:
Solve two-step word problems involving the four operations with whole numbers.
- Use estimation strategies to assess reasonableness of answers.
- Interpret remainders in word problems.
- Represent problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.

topics.name: Factors, multiples and primes
topics.description: Find factor pairs up to 50 and use them to identify multiples and prime or composite numbers.
topics.statement:
Find all factor pairs for whole numbers up to and including 50 to:
- Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors.
- Determine whether a given whole number is a multiple of a given one-digit number.
- Determine if the number is prime or composite.

topics.name: Number and shape patterns
topics.description: Generate and analyse a number or shape pattern that follows a rule.
topics.statement: Generate and analyze a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Place value to 100,000
topics.description: Explain that each place is worth ten times the place to its right in whole numbers up to 100,000.
topics.statement: Explain that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right, up to 100,000.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Read and write large numbers
topics.description: Read and write whole numbers to 100,000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
topics.statement: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers up to and including 100,000 using numerals, number names, and expanded form.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Compare multi-digit numbers
topics.description: Compare whole numbers up to 100,000 by place value and record with >, = or <.
topics.statement: Compare two multi-digit numbers up to and including 100,000 based on the values of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Standard algorithm for add and subtract
topics.description: Add and subtract whole numbers up to 100,000 with the standard algorithm and place-value understanding.
topics.statement: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers up to and including 100,000 using the standard algorithm with place value understanding.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Multi-digit multiplication
topics.description: Multiply up to three digits by one digit and two digits by two digits with area models and partial products, building toward the algorithm.
topics.statement: Multiply a whole number of up to three digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply up to two two-digit numbers with place value understanding using area models, partial products, and the properties of operations. Use models to make connections and develop the algorithm.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Division with remainders
topics.description: Divide up to three-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, finding quotients and remainders with arrays, area models and partial quotients.
topics.statement: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to three-digit dividends and one-digit divisors with place value understanding using rectangular arrays, area models, repeated subtraction, partial quotients, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division.

topics.name: Why fractions are equivalent
topics.description: Explain with area and length models why two fractions are equivalent although their parts differ.
topics.statement: Explain why a fraction is equivalent to another fraction by using area and length fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size.

topics.name: Compare unlike fractions
topics.description: Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using models, benchmarks or common terms, and justify the result.
topics.statement:
Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, using the denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions by:
- Reasoning about their size and using area and length models.
- Using benchmark fractions 0, ½, and a whole.
- Comparing common numerator or common denominators.

topics.name: Add and subtract like fractions
topics.description: Decompose fractions and add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including word problems.
topics.statement:
Understand and justify decompositions of fractions with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
- Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
- Decompose a fraction into a sum of unit fractions and a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way using area models, length models, and equations.
- Add and subtract fractions, including mixed numbers with like denominators, by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
- Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions, including mixed numbers by writing equations from a visual representation of the problem.

topics.name: Multiply a fraction by a whole
topics.description: Multiply a whole number by a fraction and solve word problems involving it.
topics.statement:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to:
- Model and explain how fractions can be represented by multiplying a whole number by a unit fraction, using this understanding to multiply a whole number by any fraction less than one.
- Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.

topics.name: Decimal notation for fractions
topics.description: Relate tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals, and add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
topics.statement:
Use decimal notation to represent fractions.
- Express, model and explain the equivalence between fractions with denominators of 10 and 100.
- Use equivalent fractions to add two fractions with denominators of 10 or 100.
- Represent tenths and hundredths with models, making connections between fractions and decimals.

topics.name: Compare decimals
topics.description: Compare decimals to hundredths by reasoning about size with models, recording with >, = or <.
topics.statement: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size using area and length models, and recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole.

topics.name: Metric measurement
topics.description: Know the relative sizes of metric units and solve one-step problems with metric length, mass and capacity.
topics.statement:
Know relative sizes of measurement units. Solve problems involving metric measurement.
- Measure to solve problems involving metric units:, centimeter, meter, gram, kilogram, Liter, milliliter.
- Add, subtract, multiply, and divide to solve one-step word problems involving whole-number measurements of length, mass, and capacity that are given in metric units.

topics.name: Convert metric units
topics.description: Convert metric measurements from a larger unit to a smaller one using place value, tables and length models.
topics.statement: Use multiplicative reasoning to convert metric measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit using place value understanding, two-column tables, and length models.

topics.name: Elapsed time across the hour
topics.description: Solve word problems adding and subtracting time intervals that cross the hour.
topics.statement: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals that cross the hour.

topics.name: Area and perimeter problems
topics.description: Find areas of rectilinear figures and solve area and perimeter problems, including fixed area or fixed perimeter.
topics.statement:
Solve problems with area and perimeter.
- Find areas of rectilinear figures with known side lengths.
- Solve problems involving a fixed area and varying perimeters and a fixed perimeter and varying areas.
- Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Line plots and data
topics.description: Collect numerical data, show it in tables, bar graphs or line plots, and tell categorical from numerical questions.
topics.statement:
Represent and interpret data using whole numbers.
- Collect data by asking a question that yields numerical data.
- Make a representation of data and interpret data in a frequency table, scaled bar graph, and/or line plot.
- Determine whether a survey question will yield categorical or numerical data.

topics.name: Angles and protractors
topics.description: Understand angles as measured in degrees, measure and sketch them with a protractor, and find unknown angles.
topics.statement:
Develop an understanding of angles and angle measurement.
- Understand angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and are measured in degrees.
- Measure and sketch angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor.
- Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Lines, rays and angles
topics.description: Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
topics.statement: Draw and identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, and perpendicular and parallel lines.

topics.name: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals
topics.description: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by angles, sides, and parallel or perpendicular lines.
topics.statement: Classify quadrilaterals and triangles based on angle measure, side lengths, and the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines.

topics.name: Lines of symmetry
topics.description: Recognise symmetry in flat figures and identify and draw lines of symmetry.
topics.statement: Recognize symmetry in a two-dimensional figure, and identify and draw lines of symmetry.

topics.name: Numerical expressions
topics.description: Write, explain and evaluate expressions with parentheses and the properties to solve up to two-step problems.
topics.statement:
Write, explain, and evaluate numerical expressions involving the four operations to solve up to two-step problems. Include expressions involving:
- Parentheses, using the order of operations
- Commutative, associative and distributive properties

topics.name: Patterns and ordered pairs
topics.description: Generate two patterns from rules, relate their terms, and graph the resulting ordered pairs.
topics.statement:
Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules.
- Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms.
- Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns.
- Graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Place value patterns
topics.description: Explain place-value patterns from millions to thousandths, including multiplying and dividing by powers of ten.
topics.statement:
Explain the patterns in the place value system from one million to the thousandths place.
- Explain that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.
- Explain patterns in products and quotients when numbers are multiplied by 1,000, 100, 10, 0.1, and 0.01 and/or divided by 10 and 100.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Decimals to thousandths
topics.description: Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths in numerals, words and expanded form.
topics.statement:
Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
- Write decimals using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
- Compare two decimals to thousandths based on the value of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Standard algorithm for multiplication
topics.description: Multiply up to a three-digit number by a two-digit number fluently with the standard algorithm.
topics.statement: Demonstrate fluency with the multiplication of two whole numbers up to a three-digit number by a two-digit number using the standard algorithm.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Divide by two-digit numbers
topics.description: Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers, finding quotients and remainders with models and partial quotients.
topics.statement: Find quotients with remainders when dividing whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors using rectangular arrays, area models, repeated subtraction, partial quotients, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Use models to make connections and develop the algorithm.

topics.unit: Number and Operations in Base Ten
topics.name: Operations with decimals
topics.description: Add, subtract, multiply and divide with decimals using models and place-value strategies, checking by estimation.
topics.statement:
Compute and solve real-world problems with multi-digit whole numbers and decimal numbers.
- Add and subtract decimals to thousandths using models, drawings or strategies based on place value.
- Multiply decimals with a product to thousandths using models, drawings, or strategies based on place value.
- Divide a whole number by a decimal and divide a decimal by a whole number, using repeated subtraction or area models. Decimals should be limited to hundredths.
- Use estimation strategies to assess reasonableness of answers.

topics.name: Add and subtract unlike fractions
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with related unlike denominators, estimating and solving word problems.
topics.statement:
Add and subtract fractions, including mixed numbers, with unlike denominators using related fractions: halves, fourths and eighths; thirds, sixths, and twelfths; fifths, tenths, and hundredths.
- Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.
- Solve one- and two-step word problems in context using area and length models to develop the algorithm. Represent the word problem in an equation.

topics.name: Fractions as division
topics.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator and solve sharing problems with fractional answers.
topics.statement:
Use fractions to model and solve division problems.
- Interpret a fraction as an equal sharing context, where a quantity is divided into equal parts.
- Model and interpret a fraction as the division of the numerator by the denominator.
- Solve one-step word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions and mixed numbers, with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12, using area, length, and set models or equations.

topics.name: Multiply fractions
topics.description: Multiply fractions and mixed numbers using area and length models, reasoning about the size of the product.
topics.statement:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including mixed numbers.
- Use area and length models to multiply two fractions, with the denominators 2, 3, 4.
- Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number and when multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.
- Solve one-step word problems involving multiplication of fractions using models to develop the algorithm.

topics.name: Divide with unit fractions
topics.description: Solve problems dividing unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions with models and equations.
topics.statement: Solve one-step word problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions using area and length models, and equations to represent the problem.

topics.name: Convert measurement units
topics.description: Use a conversion chart and multiplication to convert units within one measurement system.
topics.statement: Given a conversion chart, use multiplicative reasoning to solve one-step conversion problems within a given measurement system.

topics.name: Line graphs
topics.description: Collect data that changes over time, show and read it on a line graph, and classify survey questions by the data they yield.
topics.statement:
Represent and interpret data.
- Collect data by asking a question that yields data that changes over time.
- Make and interpret a representation of data using a line graph.
- Determine whether a survey question will yield categorical or numerical data, or data that changes over time.

topics.name: Volume with unit cubes
topics.description: Recognise volume and measure it by counting unit cubes in standard and improvised units.
topics.statement: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and measure volume by counting unit cubes, using cubic centimeters, cubic inches, cubic feet, and improvised units.

topics.name: Volume of rectangular prisms
topics.description: Relate volume to multiplication and addition, use the prism volume formula, and find volumes of two joined prisms.
topics.statement:
Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition.
- Find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths.
- Build understanding of the volume formula for rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving problems.
- Find volume of solid figures with one-digit dimensions composed of two non-overlapping rectangular prisms.

topics.name: Coordinate plane, first quadrant
topics.description: Graph points in the first quadrant and use their coordinates to solve problems.
topics.statement: Graph points in the first quadrant of a coordinate plane, and identify and interpret the x and y coordinates to solve problems.

topics.name: Hierarchy of quadrilaterals
topics.description: Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy, knowing that a category's attributes belong to all its subcategories.
topics.statement:
Classify quadrilaterals into categories based on their properties.
- Explain that attributes belonging to a category of quadrilaterals also belong to all subcategories of that category.
- Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy based on properties.

topics.name: Ratios and ratio language
topics.description: Understand a ratio as a multiplicative relationship between two quantities and model it in several ways.
topics.statement:
Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to:
- Describe a ratio as a multiplicative relationship between two quantities.
- Model a ratio relationship using a variety of representations.

topics.name: Unit ratios
topics.description: Express ratios as equivalent unit ratios and interpret both unit ratios in context.
topics.statement: Understand that ratios can be expressed as equivalent unit ratios by finding and interpreting both unit ratios in context.

topics.name: Ratio tables and reasoning
topics.description: Solve ratio problems with tables, unit ratios, measurement conversions and graphs of value pairs.
topics.statement:
Use ratio reasoning with equivalent whole-number ratios to solve real-world and mathematical problems by:
- Creating and using a table to compare ratios.
- Finding missing values in the tables.
- Using a unit ratio.
- Converting and manipulating measurements using given ratios.
- Plotting the pairs of values on the coordinate plane.

topics.name: Percent of a quantity
topics.description: Solve percent problems as ratios per 100, using benchmark percents and finding the whole from a part.
topics.statement:
Use ratio reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems with percents by:
- Understanding and finding a percent of a quantity as a ratio per 100.
- Using equivalent ratios, such as benchmark percents (50%, 25%, 10%, 5%, 1%), to determine a part of any given quantity.
- Finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

topics.name: Divide fractions
topics.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions with visual models and common denominators, including word problems.
topics.statement:
Use visual models and common denominators to:
- Interpret and compute quotients of fractions.
- Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving division of fractions.

topics.name: Long division
topics.description: Divide fluently with long division using at least four-digit dividends and interpret the quotient and remainder.
topics.statement: Fluently divide using long division with a minimum of a four-digit dividend and interpret the quotient and remainder in context.

topics.name: Decimal algorithms
topics.description: Use the standard algorithms fluently to add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals.
topics.statement: Apply and extend previous understandings of decimals to develop and fluently use the standard algorithms for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of decimals.

topics.name: Factors, GCF and LCM
topics.description: Use prime factorisation, greatest common factor and least common multiple, including with the distributive property and fractions.
topics.statement:
Understand and use prime factorization and the relationships between factors to:
- Find the unique prime factorization for a whole number.
- Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100.
- Use the greatest common factor and the distributive property to rewrite the sum of two whole numbers, each less than or equal to 100.
- Find the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12 to add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators.

topics.name: Rational numbers and absolute value
topics.description: Use positive and negative numbers for opposite quantities, explain zero in context, and interpret absolute value as magnitude.
topics.statement:
Understand and use rational numbers to:
- Describe quantities having opposite directions or values.
- Represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.
- Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line to:
- Interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world context.
- Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

topics.name: Rational numbers on a plane
topics.description: Place rational numbers on a number line and ordered pairs in the coordinate plane, relating signs to locations and reflections.
topics.statement:
Understand rational numbers as points on the number line and as ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
- a. On a number line:
- Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 and that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself.
- Find and position rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line.
- On a coordinate plane:
- Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants.
- Recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.
- Find and position pairs of rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

topics.name: Order rational numbers
topics.description: Interpret and write inequality statements about rational numbers in context and on the number line.
topics.statement:
Understand ordering of rational numbers.
- Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.
- Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

topics.name: Graph in four quadrants
topics.description: Solve problems by graphing points in all four quadrants and finding horizontal and vertical distances.
topics.statement: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

topics.name: Add and subtract integers
topics.description: Add and subtract integers from -20 to 20 with models, using zero pairs and subtraction as adding the opposite.
topics.statement:
Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction.
- Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.
- Understand p+q as the number located a distance q from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on the sign of q. Show that a number and its additive inverse create a zero pair.
- Understand subtraction of integers as adding the additive inverse, p − q = p +(–q). Show that the distance between two integers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference.
- Use models to add and subtract integers from -20 to 20 and describe real-world contexts using sums and differences.

topics.name: Expressions with exponents
topics.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions with whole-number exponents, with and without grouping symbols.
topics.statement: Write and evaluate numerical expressions, with and without grouping symbols, involving whole-number exponents.

topics.name: Algebraic expressions
topics.description: Write, read and evaluate algebraic expressions, naming their parts and substituting values from formulas.
topics.statement:
Write, read, and evaluate algebraic expressions.
- Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
- Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms and view one or more of those parts as a single entity.
- Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables using expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems.

topics.name: Generate equivalent expressions
topics.description: Use the properties of operations to write equivalent expressions without exponents.
topics.statement: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions without exponents.

topics.name: Identify equivalent expressions
topics.description: Tell when two expressions are equivalent and justify it with reasoning.
topics.statement: Identify when two expressions are equivalent and justify with mathematical reasoning.

topics.name: Solutions by substitution
topics.description: Substitute values from a set to decide which make an equation true.
topics.statement: Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation true.

topics.name: Variables in expressions
topics.description: Use variables to stand for numbers and write expressions when solving problems.
topics.statement: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem.

topics.name: One-step equations
topics.description: Write and solve equations of the form x + p = q and px = q with nonnegative rational numbers.
topics.statement:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form:
- x + p = q in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers; and,
- p ⋅ x = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

topics.name: Write and graph inequalities
topics.description: Test values in inequalities, write x > c or x < c for constraints, and graph their many solutions on a number line.
topics.statement:
Reason about inequalities by:
- Using substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an inequality true.
- Writing an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem.
- Recognizing that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions.
- Representing solutions of inequalities on number line diagrams.

topics.name: Dependent and independent variables
topics.description: Use variables for two related quantities and analyse their relationship in context, equations, tables and graphs.
topics.statement:
Represent and analyze quantitative relationships by:
- Using variables to represent two quantities in a real-world or mathematical context that change in relationship to one another.
- Analyze the relationship between quantities in different representations (context, equations, tables, and graphs).

topics.name: Area of triangles and polygons
topics.description: Find areas of triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing and decomposing them into rectangles and triangles.
topics.statement:
Create geometric models to solve real-world and mathematical problems to:
- Find the area of triangles by composing into rectangles and decomposing into right triangles.
- Find the area of special quadrilaterals and polygons by decomposing into triangles or rectangles.

topics.name: Volume with fractional edges
topics.description: Find the volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths and use it to solve problems.
topics.statement: Apply and extend previous understandings of the volume of a right rectangular prism to find the volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths. Apply this understanding to the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Polygons on the coordinate plane
topics.description: Draw polygons from vertex coordinates and find side lengths that share a coordinate.
topics.statement:
Use the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems by:
- Drawing polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices.
- Using coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

topics.name: Nets and surface area
topics.description: Represent right prisms and pyramids with nets and use them to find surface area in problems.
topics.statement: Represent right prisms and right pyramids using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Statistical questions
topics.description: Recognise a statistical question as one that expects variability in its data.
topics.statement: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

topics.name: Data distributions
topics.description: Understand that data from a statistical question has a distribution described by its centre, spread and shape.
topics.statement: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

topics.name: Centre and variability
topics.description: Describe numerical data with a measure of centre such as mean or median together with its variability.
topics.statement:
Understand that both a measure of center and a description of variability should be considered when describing a numerical data set.
- Determine the measure of center of a data set and understand that it is a single number that summarizes all the values of that data set.
- Understand that a mean is a measure of center that represents a balance point or fair share of a data set and can be influenced by the presence of extreme values within the data set.
- Understand the median as a measure of center that is the numerical middle of an ordered data set.
- Understand that describing the variability of a data set is needed to distinguish between data sets in the same scale, by comparing graphical representations of different data sets in the same scale that have similar measures of center, but different spreads.

topics.name: Dot plots, histograms, box plots
topics.description: Display numerical data in dot plots, histograms and box plots and compare what each shows.
topics.statement:
Display numerical data in plots on a number line.
- Use dot plots, histograms, and box plots to represent data.
- Compare the attributes of different representations of the same data.

topics.name: Summarize data sets
topics.description: Summarise data in context by its observations and units and by centre, variability and shape.
topics.statement:
Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.
- Describe the collected data by:
- Reporting the number of observations in dot plots and histograms.
- Communicating the nature of the attribute under investigation, how it was measured, and the units of measurement.
- Analyze center and variability by:
- Giving quantitative measures of center, describing variability, and any overall pattern, and noting any striking deviations.
- Justifying the appropriate choice of measures of center using the shape of the data distribution.

topics.name: Unit rates with fractions
topics.description: Compute unit rates from ratios of fractions to solve problems.
topics.statement: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Proportional relationships
topics.description: Recognise and represent proportional relationships with tables, graphs and equations, finding and interpreting the constant of proportionality.
topics.statement:
Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
- Understand that a proportion is a relationship of equality between ratios.
- Represent proportional relationships using tables and graphs.
- Recognize whether ratios are in a proportional relationship using tables and graphs.
- Compare two different proportional relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and verbal descriptions.
- Identify the unit rate (constant of proportionality) within two quantities in a proportional relationship using tables, graphs, equations, and verbal descriptions.
- Create equations and graphs to represent proportional relationships.
- Use a graphical representation of a proportional relationship in context to:
- Explain the meaning of any point (x, y).
- Explain the meaning of (0, 0) and why it is included.
- Understand that the y-coordinate of the ordered pair (1, r) corresponds to the unit rate and explain its meaning.

topics.name: Ratio and percent problems
topics.description: Use scale factors and unit rates to solve ratio and percent problems.
topics.statement: Use scale factors and unit rates in proportional relationships to solve ratio and percent problems.

topics.name: Add and subtract rational numbers
topics.description: Add and subtract rational numbers using properties of operations and describe real-world sums and differences.
topics.statement: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers, using the properties of operations, and describing real-world contexts using sums and differences.

topics.name: Multiply and divide rational numbers
topics.description: Multiply and divide rational numbers and convert fractions to terminating or repeating decimals by long division.
topics.statement:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division.
- Understand that a rational number is any number that can be written as a quotient of integers with a non-zero divisor.
- Apply properties of operations as strategies, including the standard algorithms, to multiply and divide rational numbers and describe the product and quotient in real-world contexts.
- Use division and previous understandings of fractions and decimals.
- Convert a fraction to a decimal using long division.
- Understand that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

topics.name: Problems with rational numbers
topics.description: Solve problems with numerical expressions involving rational numbers and all four operations.
topics.statement: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving numerical expressions with rational numbers using the four operations.

topics.name: Linear expressions
topics.description: Add, subtract, expand and factor linear expressions with rational coefficients using properties of operations.
topics.statement:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to:
- Add, subtract, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
- Factor linear expression with an integer GCF.

topics.name: Equivalent expressions in context
topics.description: See how equivalent expressions reveal relationships and interpret the parts of each in context.
topics.statement: Understand that equivalent expressions can reveal real-world and mathematical relationships. Interpret the meaning of the parts of each expression in context.

topics.name: Multi-step problems
topics.description: Solve multi-step problems with rational numbers in any form, converting between equivalent forms as needed.
topics.statement:
Solve multi-step real-world and mathematical problems posed with rational numbers in algebraic expressions.
- Apply properties of operations to calculate with positive and negative numbers in any form.
- Convert between different forms of a number and equivalent forms of the expression as appropriate.

topics.name: Equations and inequalities
topics.description: Write and solve multi-step equations and inequalities with the variable on one side, and interpret and graph the solutions.
topics.statement:
Use variables to represent quantities to solve real-world or mathematical problems.
- Construct equations to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
- Fluently solve multistep equations with the variable on one side, including those generated by word problems.
- Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
- Interpret the solution in context.
- Construct inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
- Fluently solve multi-step inequalities with the variable on one side, including those generated by word problems.
- Compare an algebraic solution process for equations and an algebraic solution process for inequalities.
- Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret in context.

topics.name: Scale drawings
topics.description: Solve problems with scale drawings, computing actual lengths and areas and creating drawings to scale.
topics.statement:
Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures by:
- Building an understanding that angle measures remain the same and side lengths are proportional.
- Using a scale factor to compute actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing.
- Creating a scale drawing.

topics.name: Constructing triangles
topics.description: Determine when given angles and sides make one, many or no triangles, and build triangles from three measures.
topics.statement: Understand the characteristics of angles and side lengths that create a unique triangle, more than one triangle or no triangle. Build triangles from three measures of angles and/or sides.

topics.name: Area and circumference of circles
topics.description: Relate radius, diameter, circumference and area, and use the circle formulas to solve problems.
topics.statement:
Understand area and circumference of a circle.
- Understand the relationships between the radius, diameter, circumference, and area.
- Apply the formulas for area and circumference of a circle to solve problems.

topics.name: Angle relationships
topics.description: Use supplementary, complementary, vertical and adjacent angles to write and solve equations for unknown angles.
topics.statement: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

topics.name: Area, volume and surface area
topics.description: Solve problems on area and perimeter of composite figures and volume and surface area of prisms and pyramids.
topics.statement:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving:
- Area and perimeter of two-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons.
- Volume and surface area of pyramids, prisms, or three-dimensional objects composed of cubes, pyramids, and right prisms.

topics.name: Samples and populations
topics.description: Use representative random samples to make valid generalisations about a population.
topics.statement:
Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by:
- Recognizing that generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population.
- Using random sampling to produce representative samples to support valid inferences.

topics.name: Inferences from samples
topics.description: Draw several random samples to gauge variation in estimates and make inferences about a population.
topics.statement: Generate multiple random samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions, and use this data to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest.

topics.name: Variability between populations
topics.description: Use mean absolute deviation, range and interquartile range, and visual overlap, to compare two data sets.
topics.statement:
Recognize the role of variability when comparing two populations.
- Calculate the measure of variability of a data set and understand that it describes how the values of the data set vary with a single number.
- Understand the mean absolute deviation of a data set is a measure of variability that describes the average distance that points within a data set are from the mean of the data set.
- Understand that the range describes the spread of the entire data set.
- Understand that the interquartile range describes the spread of the middle 50% of the data.
- Informally assess the difference between two data sets by examining the overlap and separation between the graphical representations of two data sets.

topics.name: Compare populations
topics.description: Use measures of centre and variability from random samples to compare two populations.
topics.statement: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw comparative inferences about two populations.

topics.name: Probability of events
topics.description: Understand probability as a number from 0 to 1 expressing how likely an event is.
topics.statement: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring.

topics.name: Experimental probability
topics.description: Find experimental probability from collected data and use it to predict relative frequency.
topics.statement: Collect data to calculate the experimental probability of a chance event, observing its long-run relative frequency. Use this experimental probability to predict the approximate relative frequency.

topics.name: Probability models
topics.description: Build uniform and non-uniform probability models and compare their predictions with observed frequencies.
topics.statement:
Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of simple events.
- Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
- Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by repeatedly performing a chance process and observing frequencies in the data generated.
