- Compare theoretical and experimental probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

topics.name: Compound events
topics.description: Find probabilities of compound events using lists, tables, tree diagrams and simulations.
topics.statement:
Determine probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.
- Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.
- For an event described in everyday language, identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event, when the sample space is represented using organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams.
- Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

topics.name: Irrational numbers
topics.description: Understand that every number has a decimal expansion and that irrational numbers neither terminate nor repeat.
topics.statement: Understand that every number has a decimal expansion. Building upon the definition of a rational number, know that an irrational number is defined as a non-repeating, non-terminating decimal.

topics.name: Approximate irrational numbers
topics.description: Approximate irrational numbers to compare and place them on a number line and estimate roots and pi.
topics.statement:
Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers and locate them approximately on a number line. Estimate the value of expressions involving:
- Square roots and cube roots to the tenths.
- π to the hundredths.

topics.name: Integer exponents
topics.description: Develop and apply the properties of integer exponents to write equivalent numerical expressions.
topics.statement: Develop and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

topics.name: Square and cube roots
topics.description: Use root symbols for solutions of x² = p and x³ = p and evaluate roots of perfect squares and cubes up to 400.
topics.statement:
Use square root and cube root symbols to:
- Represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number.
- Evaluate square roots of perfect squares and cube roots of perfect cubes for positive numbers less than or equal to 400.

topics.name: Scientific notation estimates
topics.description: Use scientific notation to estimate very large or small quantities and compare them.
topics.statement: Use numbers expressed in scientific notation to estimate very large or very small quantities and to express how many times as much one is than the other.

topics.name: Operations in scientific notation
topics.description: Multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation to solve problems, mixing decimal and scientific forms.
topics.statement: Perform multiplication and division with numbers expressed in scientific notation to solve real-world problems, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used.

topics.name: Multi-step linear equations
topics.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable with variables on both sides, recognising one, none or infinitely many solutions.
topics.statement:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations and inequalities in one variable.
- Recognize linear equations in one variable as having one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions.
- Solve linear equations and inequalities including multi-step equations and inequalities with the same variable on both sides.

topics.name: Systems of linear equations
topics.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in slope-intercept form by graphing or inspection and interpret the intersection.
topics.statement:
Analyze and solve a system of two linear equations in two variables in slope-intercept form.
- Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations correspond to the points of intersection of their graphs because the point of intersection satisfies both equations simultaneously.
- Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to systems of linear equations by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection

topics.name: What a function is
topics.description: Understand a function as a rule giving each input exactly one output, recognised from graphs, tables and ordered pairs.
topics.statement:
Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output.
- Recognize functions when graphed as the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and exactly one corresponding output.
- Recognize functions given a table of values or a set of ordered pairs.

topics.name: Compare linear functions
topics.description: Compare properties of two linear functions shown in different representations.
topics.statement: Compare properties of two linear functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

topics.name: Identify linear functions
topics.description: Identify linear functions from tables, equations and graphs.
topics.statement: Identify linear functions from tables, equations, and graphs.

topics.name: Model with linear functions
topics.description: Model linear relationships with y = mx + b, graph them, and interpret slope and intercept in context.
topics.statement:
Analyze functions that model linear relationships.
- Understand that a linear relationship can be generalized by y = mx + b .
- Write an equation in slope-intercept form to model a linear relationship by determining the rate of change and the initial value, given at least two (x, y) values or a graph.
- Construct a graph of a linear relationship given an equation in slope-intercept form.
- Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of the slope and y-intercept of its graph or a table of values.

topics.name: Describe functions qualitatively
topics.description: Describe where a graph increases or decreases or is linear or not, and sketch graphs from verbal descriptions.
topics.statement:
Qualitatively analyze the functional relationship between two quantities.
- Analyze a graph determining where the function is increasing or decreasing; linear or non-linear.
- Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a real-world function.

topics.name: Congruence and transformations
topics.description: Define congruence through rotations, reflections and translations and describe sequences that map one figure onto another.
topics.statement:
Use transformations to define congruence.
- Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations that create congruent figures.
- Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations.
- Given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

topics.name: Transformations with coordinates
topics.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations and reflections on figures using coordinates.
topics.statement: Describe the effect of dilations about the origin, translations, rotations about the origin in 90 degree increments, and reflections across the x-axis and y-axis on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

topics.name: Similarity and transformations
topics.description: Define similarity through transformations including dilations and describe sequences that show it.
topics.statement:
Use transformations to define similarity.
- Verify experimentally the properties of dilations that create similar figures.
- Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations.
- Given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

topics.name: Angles, transversals, triangles
topics.description: Use informal arguments about triangle angles, parallel lines cut by a transversal and angle-angle similarity.
topics.statement:
Use informal arguments to analyze angle relationships.
- Recognize relationships between interior and exterior angles of a triangle.
- Recognize the relationships between the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
- Recognize the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
- Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angles.

topics.name: Explain the Pythagorean Theorem
topics.description: Explain the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.
topics.statement: Explain the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

topics.name: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem
topics.description: Use the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve problems.
topics.statement: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Distance on the coordinate plane
topics.description: Use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points on a coordinate grid.
topics.statement: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

topics.name: Volume of cones, cylinders, spheres
topics.description: Relate the volume formulas for cones, cylinders and spheres and use them to solve problems.
topics.statement: Understand how the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres are related and use the relationship to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

topics.name: Scatter plots
topics.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots and describe clustering, outliers and types of association.
topics.statement: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Investigate and describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

topics.name: Lines of best fit
topics.description: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how well it fits.
topics.statement:
Model the relationship between bivariate quantitative data to:
- Informally fit a straight line for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.
- Informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

topics.name: Use linear models
topics.description: Solve problems with the equation of a linear model, interpreting its slope and intercept.
topics.statement: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate quantitative data, interpreting the slope and y-intercept.

topics.name: Two-way tables
topics.description: Construct and interpret two-way tables of categorical data and use relative frequencies to describe association.
topics.statement:
Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table.
- Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects.
- Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

topics.name: Integer exponent properties
topics.description: Use the properties of exponents to rewrite algebraic expressions that have integer exponents.
topics.statement: Rewrite algebraic expressions with integer exponents using the properties of exponents.

topics.name: Interpret parts of expressions
topics.description: Explain what the terms, factors, coefficients and exponents of linear, exponential and quadratic expressions mean in context, and read multi-part expressions as combinations of simpler pieces.
topics.statement:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.
a. Identify and interpret parts of a linear, exponential, or quadratic expression, including terms, factors, coefficients, and exponents.
b. Interpret a linear, exponential, or quadratic expression made of multiple parts as a combination of entities to give meaning to an expression.

topics.name: Factor quadratics to find zeros
topics.description: Factor a quadratic expression ax² + bx + c (a an integer) to reveal the solutions of the related equation or the zeros of the function.
topics.statement: Write an equivalent form of a quadratic expression ax² + bx + c, where a is an integer, by factoring to reveal the solutions of the equation or the zeros of the function the expression defines.

topics.name: Add, subtract and multiply polynomials
topics.description: See polynomial arithmetic as like integer arithmetic by adding and subtracting quadratic expressions and adding, subtracting and multiplying linear ones.
topics.statement: Build an understanding that operations with polynomials are comparable to operations with integers by adding and subtracting quadratic expressions and by adding, subtracting, and multiplying linear expressions.

topics.name: Factors, solutions and zeros
topics.description: Connect the factors of a quadratic expression with the solutions of the quadratic equation and the zeros of the quadratic function.
topics.statement: Understand the relationships among the factors of a quadratic expression, the solutions of a quadratic equation, and the zeros of a quadratic function.

topics.name: Write one-variable equations
topics.description: Write equations and inequalities in one variable for linear, exponential and quadratic situations and use them to solve problems.
topics.statement: Create equations and inequalities in one variable that represent linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships and use them to solve problems.

topics.name: Write and graph two-variable equations
topics.description: Write and graph equations in two variables that model linear, exponential and quadratic relationships between quantities.
topics.statement: Create and graph equations in two variables to represent linear, exponential, and quadratic relationships between quantities.

topics.name: Model with linear systems
topics.description: Write systems of linear equations and inequalities that model a situation in context.
topics.statement: Create systems of linear equations and inequalities to model situations in context.

topics.name: Rearrange formulas
topics.description: Solve a science or mathematics formula for a chosen quantity using the same steps as solving an equation.
topics.statement: Solve for a quantity of interest in formulas used in science and mathematics using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

topics.name: Justify solution steps
topics.description: Explain why a solution method works and justify each step when solving linear and quadratic equations.
topics.statement: Justify a chosen solution method and each step of the solving process for linear and quadratic equations using mathematical reasoning.

topics.name: Solve linear equations and inequalities
topics.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable.
topics.statement: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable.

topics.name: Solve quadratics by roots and factoring
topics.description: Find the real solutions of one-variable quadratic equations by taking square roots and by factoring.
topics.statement: Solve for the real solutions of quadratic equations in one variable by taking square roots and factoring.

topics.name: Why elimination works
topics.description: Explain why replacing an equation in a linear system with its sum with a multiple of the other equation keeps the same solutions.
topics.statement: Explain why replacing one equation in a system of linear equations by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

topics.name: Solve systems of linear equations
topics.description: Solve linear systems exactly or approximately with tables, graphs, substitution or elimination, and interpret the solutions in context.
topics.statement: Use tables, graphs, or algebraic methods (substitution and elimination) to find approximate or exact solutions to systems of linear equations and interpret solutions in terms of a context.

topics.name: Graphs as solution sets
topics.description: Recognise that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions.
topics.statement: Understand that the graph of a two variable equation represents the set of all solutions to the equation.

topics.name: Solve equations by intersecting graphs
topics.description: Explain why the x-coordinates where y = f(x) and y = g(x) meet solve f(x) = g(x) for linear, exponential and quadratic functions, and approximate them with technology or tables.
topics.statement: Build an understanding of why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of two linear, exponential, and/or quadratic equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x) and approximate solutions using graphing technology or successive approximations with a table of values.

topics.name: Graph linear inequalities
topics.description: Show the solutions of a linear inequality or a system of linear inequalities as a region of the coordinate plane.
topics.statement: Represent the solutions of a linear inequality or a system of linear inequalities graphically as a region of the plane.

topics.name: What a function is
topics.description: Understand a function as assigning each input in the domain exactly one output in the range, with f(x) as the output for x and the graph of f as the graph of y = f(x).
topics.statement:
Build an understanding that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range by recognizing that:
- if f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x.
- the graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

topics.name: Use function notation
topics.description: Evaluate linear, quadratic and exponential functions written in function notation and interpret statements in that notation in context.
topics.statement: Use function notation to evaluate linear, quadratic, and exponential functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

topics.name: Sequences as functions
topics.description: See arithmetic and geometric sequences, defined recursively or explicitly, as functions on the integers related to linear and exponential functions.
topics.statement: Recognize that recursively and explicitly defined sequences are functions whose domain is a subset of the integers, the terms of an arithmetic sequence are a subset of the range of a linear function, and the terms of a geometric sequence are a subset of the range of an exponential function.

topics.name: Key features in context
topics.description: Interpret intercepts, increasing or decreasing and positive or negative intervals, and maximums and minimums of functions given by graphs, tables or descriptions in context.
topics.statement: Interpret key features of graphs, tables, and verbal descriptions in context to describe functions that arise in applications relating two quantities, including: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; and maximums and minimums.

topics.name: Domain and range in context
topics.description: Relate a function's domain and range to its graph and to the real situation it describes.
topics.statement: Interpret a function in terms of the context by relating its domain and range to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

topics.name: Average rate of change
topics.description: Calculate and interpret a function's average rate of change over an interval from a table, graph or formula.
topics.statement: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change over a specified interval for a function presented numerically, graphically, and/or symbolically.

topics.name: Graph functions to show features
topics.description: Represent linear, exponential and quadratic functions in different ways, by hand or with technology, to show domain, range, rate of change, intercepts, intervals, extremes and end behavior.
topics.statement: Analyze linear, exponential, and quadratic functions by generating different representations, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases, to show key features, including: domain and range; rate of change; intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; maximums and minimums; and end behavior.

topics.name: Equivalent forms reveal properties
topics.description: Rewrite quadratic functions to reveal key features, and interpret growth and decay rates of exponential functions.
topics.statement:
Use equivalent expressions to reveal and explain different properties of a function.
a. Rewrite a quadratic function to reveal and explain different key features of the function
b. Interpret and explain growth and decay rates for an exponential function.

topics.name: Compare functions across representations
topics.description: Compare key features of two linear, quadratic or exponential functions given in different representations.
topics.statement: Compare key features of two functions (linear, quadratic, or exponential) each with a different representation (symbolically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

topics.name: Build functions from relationships
topics.description: Write linear and exponential functions, including sequences, from graphs, descriptions or two points, and combine functions by adding, subtracting or multiplying two linear ones.
topics.statement:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
a. Build linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two ordered pairs (include reading these from a table).
b. Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities by combining linear, exponential, or quadratic functions with addition and subtraction or two linear functions with multiplication.

topics.name: Explicit and recursive sequences
topics.description: Move between explicit and recursive forms of arithmetic and geometric sequences and use both to model situations.
topics.statement: Translate between explicit and recursive forms of arithmetic and geometric sequences and use both to model situations.

topics.name: Linear or exponential model
topics.description: Decide whether a situation is linear or exponential by looking at change over equal intervals, and justify the choice of model.
topics.statement: Identify situations that can be modeled with linear and exponential functions, and justify the most appropriate model for a situation based on the rate of change over equal intervals.

topics.name: Exponential growth overtakes
topics.description: Use graphs and tables to show that exponential growth eventually exceeds linear or quadratic growth.
topics.statement: Compare the end behavior of linear, exponential, and quadratic functions using graphs and tables to show that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly or quadratically.

topics.name: Interpret function parameters
topics.description: Explain in context what the parameters mean in a linear function ax + b or an exponential function a times b to the x.
topics.statement: Interpret the parameters a and b in a linear function f(x) = ax + b or an exponential function g(x) = abˣ in terms of a context.

topics.name: Coordinate geometry of polygons
topics.description: Use coordinates to find perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, and to classify triangles and quadrilaterals algebraically.
topics.statement:
Use coordinates to solve geometric problems involving polygons algebraically
- Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles.
- Use coordinates to verify algebraically that a given set of points produces a particular type of triangle or quadrilateral.

topics.name: Slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines
topics.description: Use coordinates to justify the slope rules for parallel and perpendicular lines, classify pairs of lines, and write equations of such lines through a point.
topics.statement:
Use coordinates to prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve problems.
- Determine if two lines are parallel, perpendicular, or neither.
- Find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point.

topics.name: Midpoints and endpoints
topics.description: Use coordinates to find the midpoint or a missing endpoint of a line segment.
topics.statement: Use coordinates to find the midpoint or endpoint of a line segment.

topics.name: Histograms and box plots
topics.description: Use technology to display data on a number line with histograms and box plots.
topics.statement: Use technology to represent data with plots on the real number line (histograms, and box plots).

topics.name: Compare center and spread
topics.description: Choose suitable statistics to compare the center and spread of two or more data sets, and interpret differences in shape, center and spread in context.
topics.statement: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets. Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets.

topics.name: Effect of outliers
topics.description: Examine how outliers change the shape, center and spread of a data set.
topics.statement: Examine the effects of extreme data points (outliers) on shape, center, and/or spread.

topics.name: Scatter plots and fitted lines
topics.description: Plot two quantitative variables, fit least squares lines and exponential models with technology, use them to solve problems, and judge linear fit with residuals.
topics.statement:
Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.
a. Fit a least squares regression line to linear data using technology. Use the fitted function to solve problems.
b. Assess the fit of a linear function by analyzing residuals.
c. Fit a function to exponential data using technology. Use the fitted function to solve problems.

topics.name: Interpret linear models
topics.description: Interpret the slope and intercept of a linear model in context, use it to interpolate and extrapolate, and judge whether a prediction is valid.
topics.statement: Interpret in context the rate of change and the intercept of a linear model. Use the linear model to interpolate and extrapolate predicted values. Assess the validity of a predicted value.

topics.name: Correlation and residual plots
topics.description: Describe relationships between two variables, compute and interpret the correlation coefficient, and use scatter plots, correlation and residuals to judge whether a linear model fits.
topics.statement: Analyze patterns and describe relationships between two variables in context. Using technology, determine the correlation coefficient of bivariate data and interpret it as a measure of the strength and direction of a linear relationship. Use a scatter plot, correlation coefficient, and a residual plot to determine the appropriateness of using a linear function to model a relationship between two variables.

topics.name: Association versus causation
topics.description: Tell the difference between two variables being associated and one causing the other.
topics.statement: Distinguish between association and causation.

topics.name: Rational exponents as radicals
topics.description: Explain how an expression with a rational exponent can be written as a radical expression.
topics.statement: Explain how expressions with rational exponents can be rewritten as radical expressions.

topics.name: Rewrite radicals and rational exponents
topics.description: Use exponent properties to rewrite expressions with radicals and rational exponents into equivalent forms.
topics.statement: Rewrite expressions with radicals and rational exponents into equivalent expressions using the properties of exponents.

topics.name: Rational and irrational sums, products
topics.description: Explain why sums and products of rationals are rational, while a rational plus an irrational, or a nonzero rational times an irrational, is irrational.

topics.name: Complex numbers
topics.description: Know that i squared is -1 and that every complex number can be written as a + bi with a and b real.
topics.statement: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = – 1, and every complex number has the form a + bi where a and b are real numbers.

topics.name: Interpret quadratic and radical expressions
topics.description: Interpret the parts of quadratic, square root, inverse variation and right-triangle trigonometric expressions, and read multi-part expressions as single entities in context.
topics.statement:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.
a. Identify and interpret parts of a quadratic, square root, inverse variation, or right triangle trigonometric expression, including terms, factors, coefficients, radicands, and exponents.
b. Interpret quadratic and square root expressions made of multiple parts as a combination of single entities to give meaning in terms of a context.

topics.name: Complete the square
topics.description: Complete the square on a quadratic expression ax² + bx + c to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function.
topics.statement: Write an equivalent form of a quadratic expression by completing the square, where a is an integer of a quadratic expression, ax² + bx + c, to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function the expression defines.

topics.name: Polynomial arithmetic
topics.description: Add, subtract and multiply polynomials, seeing the parallel with integer arithmetic.
topics.statement: Extend the understanding that operations with polynomials are comparable to operations with integers by adding, subtracting, and multiplying polynomials.

topics.name: Write one-variable equations
topics.description: Write equations and inequalities in one variable for quadratic, square root, inverse variation and right-triangle trigonometric situations and solve problems with them.
topics.statement: Create equations and inequalities in one variable that represent quadratic, square root, inverse variation, and right triangle trigonometric relationships and use them to solve problems.

topics.name: Write and graph two-variable equations
topics.description: Write and graph two-variable equations for quadratic, square root and inverse variation relationships.
topics.statement: Create and graph equations in two variables to represent quadratic, square root and inverse variation relationships between quantities.

topics.name: Model with systems of equations
topics.description: Write systems of linear, quadratic, square root and inverse variation equations that model a situation.
topics.statement: Create systems of linear, quadratic, square root, and inverse variation equations to model situations in context.

topics.name: Justify solution steps
topics.description: Justify a solution method and each step when solving quadratic, square root and inverse variation equations.
topics.statement: Justify a chosen solution method and each step of the solving process for quadratic, square root and inverse variation equations using mathematical reasoning.

topics.name: Radical and inverse variation equations
topics.description: Solve square root and inverse variation equations in context, interpret the results, and explain how extraneous solutions arise.
topics.statement: Solve and interpret one variable inverse variation and square root equations arising from a context, and explain how extraneous solutions may be produced.

topics.name: Quadratic formula and complex solutions
topics.description: Solve any quadratic equation, seeing the quadratic formula as completing the square in general, and express non-real solutions as a ± bi.
topics.statement:
Solve for all solutions of quadratic equations in one variable.
a. Understand that the quadratic formula is the generalization of solving ax² + bx + c by using the process of completing the square.
b. Explain when quadratic equations will have non-real solutions and express complex solutions as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

topics.name: Linear-quadratic systems
topics.description: Solve systems of a linear and a quadratic equation with tables, graphs or algebra, and interpret the solutions in context.
topics.statement: Use tables, graphs, and algebraic methods to approximate or find exact solutions of systems of linear and quadratic equations, and interpret the solutions in terms of a context.

topics.name: Solve equations by intersecting graphs
topics.description: Explain why intersections of y = f(x) and y = g(x) solve f(x) = g(x) for square root and inverse variation equations, and approximate them with technology or tables.
topics.statement: Extend the understanding that the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of two square root and/or inverse variation equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x) and approximate solutions using graphing technology or successive approximations with a table of values.

topics.name: Transformations as functions
topics.description: Treat a geometric transformation as a function whose domain and range are sets of points and whose image depends on the pre-image.

topics.name: Function notation for transformations
topics.description: Use function notation to describe the image of a figure under a translation, a rotation by multiples of 90 degrees, a reflection over an axis, or a dilation.
topics.statement: Extend the use of function notation to express the image of a geometric figure in the plane resulting from a translation, rotation by multiples of 90 degrees about the origin, reflection across an axis, or dilation as a function of its pre-image.

topics.name: Key features in context
topics.description: Interpret domain, range, rate of change, symmetry and end behavior of functions given by graphs, tables or descriptions in context.
topics.statement: Interpret key features of graphs, tables, and verbal descriptions in context to describe functions that arise in applications relating two quantities, including: domain and range, rate of change, symmetries, and end behavior.

topics.name: Graph functions to show features
topics.description: Represent quadratic, square root and inverse variation functions in different ways to show domain, range, intercepts, intervals, rate of change, extremes, symmetry and end behavior.
topics.statement: Analyze quadratic, square root, and inverse variation functions by generating different representations, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases, to show key features, including: domain and range; intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; rate of change; maximums and minimums; symmetries; and end behavior.

topics.name: Completing the square for features
topics.description: Complete the square on a quadratic function to find its zeros, extreme value and symmetry, and interpret them in context.
topics.statement: Use equivalent expressions to reveal and explain different properties of a function by developing and using the process of completing the square to identify the zeros, extreme values, and symmetry in graphs and tables representing quadratic functions, and interpret these in terms of a context.

topics.name: Compare functions across representations
topics.description: Compare key features of two linear, quadratic, square root or inverse variation functions given in different representations.
topics.statement: Compare key features of two functions (linear, quadratic, square root, or inverse variation functions) each with a different representation (symbolically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

topics.name: Build quadratic and inverse variation functions
topics.description: Write quadratic functions with real solutions and inverse variation functions from a graph, a description or ordered pairs.
topics.statement: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities by building quadratic functions with real solution(s) and inverse variation functions given a graph, a description of a relationship, or ordered pairs (include reading these from a table).

topics.name: Transformations of function graphs
topics.description: Describe how k times f(x), f(x) + k and f(x + k) change the graph and table of linear, quadratic, square root and inverse variation functions.
topics.statement: Understand the effects of the graphical and tabular representations of a linear, quadratic, square root, and inverse variation function f with k ∙ f(x), f(x) + k, f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative).

topics.name: Rigid motions and dilations
topics.description: Represent transformations in the plane, compare rigid motions with transformations that change size, and connect rigid motions with congruence and dilations with similarity.
topics.statement:
Experiment with transformations in the plane.
- Represent transformations in the plane.
- Compare rigid motions that preserve distance and angle measure (translations, reflections, rotations) to transformations that do not preserve both distance and angle measure (e.g. stretches, dilations).
- Understand that rigid motions produce congruent figures while dilations produce similar figures.

topics.name: Symmetry of polygons
topics.description: Describe the reflection and rotation symmetries of triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons, naming centers, angles and lines of symmetry.
topics.statement: Given a triangle, quadrilateral, or regular polygon, describe any reflection or rotation symmetry i.e., actions that carry the figure onto itself. Identify center and angle(s) of rotation symmetry. Identify line(s) of reflection symmetry.

topics.name: Properties of rigid motions
topics.description: Verify by experiment how rotations, reflections and translations act on angles, circles, perpendicular and parallel lines and segments.
topics.statement: Verify experimentally properties of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

topics.name: Perform and describe rigid motions
topics.description: Find the image of a figure under a rigid motion, and name a rigid motion or sequence that maps a figure onto a given image.
topics.statement: Given a geometric figure and a rigid motion, find the image of the figure. Given a geometric figure and its image, specify a rigid motion or sequence of rigid motions that will transform the pre-image to its image.

topics.name: Congruence by rigid motions
topics.description: Decide whether two figures are congruent by finding rigid motions that map one onto the other.
topics.statement: Determine whether two figures are congruent by specifying a rigid motion or sequence of rigid motions that will transform one figure onto the other.

topics.name: Congruent triangles and rigid motions
topics.description: Use rigid motions to show that triangles are congruent exactly when all corresponding sides and angles are congruent.
topics.statement: Use the properties of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

topics.name: Triangle congruence criteria
topics.description: Justify ASA, SAS and SSS with rigid motions, and use ASA, SAS, SSS and HL to decide whether triangles are congruent.
topics.statement: Use congruence in terms of rigid motion. Justify the ASA, SAS, and SSS criteria for triangle congruence. Use criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, SSS, HL) to determine whether two triangles are congruent.

topics.name: Theorems about lines and angles
topics.description: Prove and use theorems on vertical angles, angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal, perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors.
topics.statement:
Prove theorems about lines and angles and use them to prove relationships in geometric figures including:
- Vertical angles are congruent.
- When a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent.
- When a transversal crosses parallel lines, corresponding angles are congruent.
- Points are on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment if and only if they are equidistant from the endpoints of the segment.
- Use congruent triangles to justify why the bisector of an angle is equidistant from the sides of the angle

topics.name: Theorems about triangles
topics.description: Prove and use triangle theorems: the angle sum, exterior angles, isosceles base angles and the midsegment.
topics.statement:
Prove theorems about triangles and use them to prove relationships in geometric figures including:
- The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a triangle is 180º.
- An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its remote interior angles.
- The base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent.
- The segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length.

topics.name: Properties of dilations
topics.description: Verify by experiment that dilations keep lines parallel or on the same line, scale lengths and distances from the center by the scale factor, and preserve angles.
topics.statement:
Verify experimentally the properties of dilations with given center and scale factor:
a. When a line segment passes through the center of dilation, the line segment and its image lie on the same line. When a line segment does not pass through the center of dilation, the line segment and its image are parallel.
b. The length of the image of a line segment is equal to the length of the line segment multiplied by the scale factor.
c. The distance between the center of a dilation and any point on the image is equal to the scale factor multiplied by the distance between the dilation center and the corresponding point on the pre-image.
d. Dilations preserve angle measure.

topics.name: Similarity through transformations
topics.description: Decide whether figures are similar by finding a sequence of transformations, and use dilations to show triangles with proportional sides and congruent angles are similar.
topics.statement:
Understand similarity in terms of transformations.
a. Determine whether two figures are similar by specifying a sequence of transformations that will transform one figure into the other.
b. Use the properties of dilations to show that two triangles are similar when all corresponding pairs of sides are proportional and all corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

topics.name: AA similarity
topics.description: Use rigid motions and dilations to justify the angle-angle criterion for similar triangles.
topics.statement: Use transformations (rigid motions and dilations) to justify the AA criterion for triangle similarity.

topics.name: Similarity theorems for triangles
topics.description: Use similarity to prove triangle theorems, including the side-splitter theorem and its converse and the Pythagorean Theorem, and solve problems with them.
topics.statement:
Use similarity to solve problems and to prove theorems about triangles. Use theorems about triangles to prove relationships in geometric figures.
- A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally and its converse.
- The Pythagorean Theorem

topics.name: Defining trigonometric ratios
topics.description: Discover that side ratios in similar right triangles depend only on the angles, and use this to define the trigonometric ratios for acute angles.
topics.statement: Verify experimentally that the side ratios in similar right triangles are properties of the angle measures in the triangle, due to the preservation of angle measure in similarity. Use this discovery to develop definitions of the trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

topics.name: Solve right triangles
topics.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right-triangle problems in context.
topics.statement: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve problems involving right triangles in terms of a context

topics.name: Special right triangles
topics.description: Develop the properties of 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles and use them to solve problems.
topics.statement: Develop properties of special right triangles (45-45-90 and 30-60-90) and use them to solve problems.

topics.name: Simulation and theoretical probability
topics.description: Use simulation to judge whether an experimental probability from sample data is consistent with the theoretical probability.
topics.statement: Use simulation to determine whether the experimental probability generated by sample data is consistent with the theoretical probability based on known information about the population.

topics.name: Events and sample spaces
topics.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space, or as unions, intersections and complements of other events.
topics.statement: Describe events as subsets of the outcomes in a sample space using characteristics of the outcomes or as unions, intersections and complements of other events.

topics.name: Independence and conditional probability
topics.description: Use two-way tables to understand P(A|B) as the share of B's outcomes also in A, and understand A as independent of B when P(A|B) equals P(A).
topics.statement:
Develop and understand independence and conditional probability.
a. Use a 2-way table to develop understanding of the conditional probability of A given B (written P(A|B)) as the likelihood that A will occur given that B has occurred. That is, P(A|B) is the fraction of event B’s outcomes that also belong to event A.
b. Understand that event A is independent from event B if the probability of event A does not change in response to the occurrence of event B. That is P(A|B)=P(A).

topics.name: Two-way frequency tables
topics.description: Build two-way tables for two categorical variables, use them to find conditional, joint and marginal probabilities, and test events for independence.
topics.statement: Represent data on two categorical variables by constructing a two-way frequency table of data. Interpret the two-way table as a sample space to calculate conditional, joint and marginal probabilities. Use the table to decide if events are independent.

topics.name: Conditional probability in everyday language
topics.description: Recognise and explain conditional probability and independence in everyday situations and language.
topics.statement: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

topics.name: Find conditional probabilities
topics.description: Find the probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that are also in A, and interpret it in context.
topics.statement: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B’s outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in context.

topics.name: The Addition Rule
topics.description: Use the Addition Rule for P(A or B) and interpret the result in context.
topics.statement: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in context.

topics.name: The Multiplication Rule
topics.description: Use the general Multiplication Rule for P(A and B), including the independent case, and interpret the result in context.
topics.statement: Apply the general Multiplication Rule P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in context. Include the case where A and B are independent: P(A and B) = P(A) P(B).

topics.name: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
topics.description: Use the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to find how many solutions a polynomial has and what kinds they might be.
topics.statement: Use the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to determine the number and potential types of solutions for polynomial functions.

topics.name: Interpret advanced expressions
topics.description: Interpret the parts of piecewise, absolute value, polynomial, exponential and rational expressions, and read multi-part expressions as single entities in context.
topics.statement:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.
a. Identify and interpret parts of a piecewise, absolute value, polynomial, exponential and rational expressions including terms, factors, coefficients, and exponents.
b. Interpret expressions composed of multiple parts by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity to give meaning in terms of a context.

topics.name: Use structure to rewrite expressions
topics.description: Use the structure of an expression to find ways to write it in equivalent forms.
topics.statement: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to write equivalent expressions.

topics.name: Rewrite exponential expressions
topics.description: Use exponent properties to rewrite exponential expressions so they show rates over different time intervals.
topics.statement: Write an equivalent form of an exponential expression by using the properties of exponents to transform expressions to reveal rates based on different intervals of the domain.

topics.name: The Remainder Theorem
topics.description: Understand the Remainder Theorem and use it.
topics.statement: Understand and apply the Remainder Theorem.

topics.name: Polynomial factors and zeros
topics.description: Connect the factors of a polynomial with the solutions of the polynomial equation and the zeros of the function.
topics.statement: Understand the relationship among factors of a polynomial expression, the solutions of a polynomial equation and the zeros of a polynomial function.

topics.name: Rewrite rational expressions
topics.description: Rewrite a simple rational expression a(x)/b(x) as a quotient plus a remainder over b(x), with the remainder of lower degree than b(x).
topics.statement: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x).

topics.name: Rational expression arithmetic
topics.description: Treat rational expressions like rational numbers: add and subtract ones with linear denominators, and multiply and divide them.
topics.statement:
Understand the similarities between arithmetic with rational expressions and arithmetic with rational numbers.
a. Add and subtract two rational expressions, a(x) and b(x), where the denominators of both a(x) and b(x) are linear expressions.
b. Multiply and divide two rational expressions.

topics.name: Write one-variable equations
topics.description: Write equations and inequalities in one variable for absolute value, polynomial, exponential and rational situations and solve them algebraically and graphically.
topics.statement: Create equations and inequalities in one variable that represent absolute value, polynomial, exponential, and rational relationships and use them to solve problems algebraically and graphically.

topics.name: Write and graph two-variable equations
topics.description: Write and graph two-variable equations for absolute value, polynomial, exponential and rational relationships.
topics.statement: Create and graph equations in two variables to represent absolute value, polynomial, exponential and rational relationships between quantities.

topics.name: Model with systems
topics.description: Write systems of equations or inequalities that model a situation in context.
topics.statement: Create systems of equations and/or inequalities to model situations in context.

topics.name: Justify solution steps
topics.description: Justify a solution method and explain each step of solving an equation.
topics.statement: Justify a solution method for equations and explain each step of the solving process using mathematical reasoning.

topics.name: Solve rational equations
topics.description: Solve one-variable rational equations in context, interpret the solutions, and explain how extraneous solutions arise.
topics.statement: Solve and interpret one variable rational equations arising from a context, and explain how extraneous solutions may be produced.

topics.name: Solve equations by intersecting graphs
topics.description: Explain why intersections of y = f(x) and y = g(x) solve f(x) = g(x), and approximate those solutions with technology or tables.
topics.statement: Extend an understanding that the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of two equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x) and approximate solutions using a graphing technology or successive approximations with a table of values.

topics.name: Trigonometric ratios as functions
topics.description: Recognise trigonometric ratios as functions of angle measure.
topics.statement: Extend the concept of a function by recognizing that trigonometric ratios are functions of angle measure.

topics.name: Piecewise function notation
topics.description: Evaluate piecewise functions written in function notation and interpret such statements in context.
topics.statement: Use function notation to evaluate piecewise defined functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

topics.name: Periodicity and discontinuities
topics.description: Interpret key features of functions in context from graphs, tables and descriptions, including periodicity and discontinuities.
topics.statement: Interpret key features of graphs, tables, and verbal descriptions in context to describe functions that arise in applications relating two quantities to include periodicity and discontinuities.

topics.name: Graph advanced functions
topics.description: Represent piecewise, absolute value, polynomial, exponential, rational, sine and cosine functions to show key features such as intercepts, extremes, symmetry, end behavior, period and discontinuities.
topics.statement: Analyze piecewise, absolute value, polynomials, exponential, rational, and trigonometric functions (sine and cosine) using different representations to show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases, including: domain and range; intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; rate of change; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; period; and discontinuities.

topics.name: Compare functions across representations
topics.description: Compare key features of two different functions, each given in a different representation.
topics.statement: Compare key features of two functions using different representations by comparing properties of two different functions, each with a different representation (symbolically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

topics.name: Build polynomial and exponential functions
topics.description: Write polynomial and exponential functions from graphs, descriptions or points, and combine standard function types with arithmetic operations in context.
topics.statement:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
a. Build polynomial and exponential functions with real solution(s) given a graph, a description of a relationship, or ordered pairs (include reading these from a table).
b. Build a new function, in terms of a context, by combining standard function types using arithmetic operations.

topics.name: Transformations including horizontal stretch
topics.description: Describe how k times f(x), f(x) + k, f(x + k) and f(kx) change a function's graph and table for positive and negative k.
topics.statement: Extend an understanding of the effects on the graphical and tabular representations of a function when replacing f(x) with k ∙f(x), f(x) + k, f(x + k) to include f(k ∙ x) for specific values of k (both positive and negative).

topics.name: Inverse functions
topics.description: Understand inverse pairs such as exponential and logarithmic, decide whether an inverse exists, and represent and use the inverse of linear, quadratic or exponential functions in context.
topics.statement:
Find an inverse function.
a. Understand the inverse relationship between exponential and logarithmic, quadratic and square root, and linear to linear functions and use this relationship to solve problems using tables, graphs, and equations.
b. Determine if an inverse function exists by analyzing tables, graphs, and equations.
c. If an inverse function exists for a linear, quadratic and/or exponential function, f, represent the inverse function, f-1, with a table, graph, or equation and use it to solve problems in terms of a context.

topics.name: Exponential beats polynomial growth
topics.description: Compare rates of change over equal intervals to show exponential growth eventually exceeds polynomial growth.
topics.statement: Compare the end behavior of functions using their rates of change over intervals of the same length to show that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing as a polynomial function.

topics.name: Solve exponentials with logarithms
topics.description: Write the solution of an exponential equation as a logarithm and evaluate it with technology.
topics.statement: Use logarithms to express the solution to abᶜᵗ = d where a, b, c, and d are numbers and evaluate the logarithm using technology.

topics.name: Radian measure
topics.description: Understand a radian as arc length divided by radius, a real number that serves as the domain of trigonometric functions.
topics.statement:
Understand radian measure of an angle as:
- The ratio of the length of an arc on a circle subtended by the angle to its radius.
- A dimensionless measure of length defined by the quotient of arc length and radius that is a real number.
- The domain for trigonometric functions

topics.name: Unit circle sine and cosine
topics.description: Represent sine and cosine with tables, graphs and technology, reading them as the y- and x-coordinates of a point on the unit circle at a given radian angle.
topics.statement:
Build an understanding of trigonometric functions by using tables, graphs and technology to represent the cosine and sine functions.
a. Interpret the sine function as the relationship between the radian measure of an angle formed by the horizontal axis and a terminal ray on the unit circle and its y coordinate.
b. Interpret the cosine function as the relationship between the radian measure of an angle formed by the horizontal axis and a terminal ray on the unit circle and its x coordinate.

topics.name: Model periodic phenomena
topics.description: Use technology to explore the parameters of f(x) = a sin(bx) + h, model periodic situations, and interpret key features in context.
topics.statement: Use technology to investigate the parameters, a, b, and ℎ of a sine function, f(x) = a ∙ sin(b ∙ x) + ℎ, to represent periodic phenomena and interpret key features in terms of a context.

topics.name: Centers of triangles
topics.description: Verify by experiment the properties of a triangle's centroid, incenter and circumcenter.
topics.statement: Verify experimentally properties of the centers of triangles (centroid, incenter, and circumcenter).

topics.name: Theorems about parallelograms
topics.description: Prove that a parallelogram's opposite sides and angles are congruent, its diagonals bisect each other, and congruent diagonals make it a rectangle.
topics.statement:
Prove theorems about parallelograms.
- Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent.
- Opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent.
- Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
- If the diagonals of a parallelogram are congruent, then the parallelogram is a rectangle.

topics.name: Prove theorems about figures
topics.description: Use properties, definitions and theorems of two-dimensional figures to prove theorems and solve problems.
topics.statement: Apply properties, definitions, and theorems of two-dimensional figures to prove geometric theorems and solve problems.

topics.name: Circle theorems
topics.description: Understand and apply theorems about angles in circles (central, inscribed, circumscribed) and about radii, diameters, secants, tangents and chords.
topics.statement:
Understand and apply theorems about circles.
- Understand and apply theorems about relationships with angles and circles, including central, inscribed and circumscribed angles.
- Understand and apply theorems about relationships with line segments and circles including, radii, diameter, secants, tangents and chords.

topics.name: Arc length and sectors
topics.description: Use similarity to show arc length is proportional to radius, define radian measure as arc over radius, and find arc lengths and sector areas.
topics.statement: Using similarity, demonstrate that the length of an arc, s, for a given central angle is proportional to the radius, r, of the circle. Define radian measure of the central angle as the ratio of the length of the arc to the radius of the circle, s/r. Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

topics.name: Equation of a circle
topics.description: Derive the equation of a circle from its center and radius with the Pythagorean Theorem, and complete the square to find the center and radius from an equation.
topics.statement: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

topics.name: Volume formulas
topics.description: Use the volume formulas for prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres to solve problems.
topics.statement: Use the volume formulas for prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

topics.name: Cross-sections and solids of rotation
topics.description: Identify two-dimensional cross-sections of solids and the solids formed by rotating two-dimensional shapes.
topics.statement: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

topics.name: Modeling with geometry
topics.description: Model real objects and relationships with shapes, formulas and functions, and solve density, design and optimization problems.
topics.statement:
Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
- Use geometric and algebraic concepts to solve problems in modeling situations:
- Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties, to model real-life objects.
- Use geometric formulas and algebraic functions to model relationships.
- Apply concepts of density based on area and volume.
- Apply geometric concepts to solve design and optimization problems.

topics.name: Inference from random samples
topics.description: Understand how inferences about a population are drawn from a random sample of it.
topics.statement: Understand the process of making inferences about a population based on a random sample from that population.

topics.name: Surveys, experiments and observational studies
topics.description: Recognise the purposes of and differences between sample surveys, experiments and observational studies, and how each should use randomization.
topics.statement: Recognize the purposes of and differences between sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies and understand how randomization should be used in each.

topics.name: Estimate with margin of error
topics.description: Use simulation to see how samples estimate a population mean or proportion and how to find a margin of error.
topics.statement: Use simulation to understand how samples can be used to estimate a population mean or proportion and how to determine a margin of error for the estimate.

topics.name: Compare populations by simulation
topics.description: Use simulation to decide whether differences between samples from two populations show a real difference in a parameter.
topics.statement: Use simulation to determine whether observed differences between samples from two distinct populations indicate that the two populations are actually different in terms of a parameter of interest.

topics.name: Evaluate reports of data
topics.description: Evaluate articles and websites that report data by checking the data source, the study design and how the data are displayed.
topics.statement: Evaluate articles and websites that report data by identifying the source of the data, the design of the study, and the way the data are graphically displayed.

topics.name: Complex number operations
topics.description: Apply the properties of complex numbers to operate with them. Covers adding, subtracting and multiplying complex numbers.
topics.statement: Apply properties and operations with complex numbers.

objectives.statement: Execute procedures to add and subtract complex numbers.
Execute procedures to multiply complex numbers.

topics.name: Matrix and vector operations
topics.description: Apply the properties of operations with matrices and vectors. Covers matrix addition, subtraction, multiplication and scalar multiplication, and vector addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication.
topics.statement: Apply properties and operations with matrices and vectors.

objectives.statement: Execute procedures of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and scalar multiplication on matrices.
Execute procedures of addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication on vectors.

topics.name: Function composition
topics.description: Build new functions by composing existing ones. Covers composing two functions algebraically, and evaluating a composite function from algebraic, graphical or tabular forms.
topics.statement: Apply properties of function composition to build new functions from existing functions.

objectives.statement: Execute algebraic procedures to compose two functions.
Execute a procedure to determine the value of a composite function at a given value when the functions are in algebraic, graphical, or tabular representations.

topics.name: Trigonometric identities and laws
topics.description: Apply trigonometry to solve problems. Covers reciprocal and Pythagorean identities, the Law of Sines and Law of Cosines, and key features of sine and cosine models in context.
topics.statement: Apply properties of trigonometry to solve problems.

objectives.statement: Translate trigonometric expressions using the reciprocal and Pythagorean identities.
Implement the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to solve problems.
Interpret key features (amplitude, period, phase shift, vertical shifts, midline, domain, range) of models using sine and cosine functions in terms of a context.

topics.name: Logarithmic functions
topics.description: Apply the properties and key features of logarithmic functions. Covers simplifying and solving with logarithm properties, solving equations in context, and interpreting key features across representations.
topics.statement: Apply the properties and key features of logarithmic functions.

objectives.statement: Execute properties of logarithms to simplify and solve equations algebraically.
Implement properties of logarithms to solve equations in contextual situations.
Interpret key features of a logarithmic function using multiple representations.

topics.name: Piecewise functions
topics.description: Understand the properties and key features of piecewise functions. Covers moving between algebraic and graphical forms, and building piecewise models of situations.
topics.statement: Understand the properties and key features of piecewise functions.

objectives.statement: Translate between algebraic and graphical representations of piecewise functions (linear, exponential, quadratic, polynomial, square root).
Construct piecewise functions to model a contextual situation.

topics.name: Regression models
topics.description: Model bivariate data with regression functions. Covers linear, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic and sinusoidal regression with technology, and judging fit of non-linear models with residuals.
topics.statement: Understand how to model functions with regression.

objectives.statement: Construct regression models of linear, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic, & sinusoidal functions of bivariate data using technology to model data and solve problems.
Compare residuals and residual plots of non-linear models to assess the goodness-of-fit of the model.

topics.name: Statistical investigations
topics.description: Plan and carry out statistical investigations of real-world questions. Covers statistical questions, designing surveys and experiments, organising large datasets with technology, and reading non-standard data displays.
topics.statement: Create statistical investigations to make sense of real world phenomenon.

objectives.statement: Construct statistical questions to guide explorations of data in context.
Design sample surveys and comparative experiments using sampling methods to collect and analyze data to answer a statistical question.

Organize large datasets of real world contexts (i.e. datasets that include 3 or more measures and have sample sizes >200) using technology (e.g., spreadsheets, dynamic data analysis tools) to determine: types of variables in the data set, possible outcomes for each variable, statistical questions that could be asked of the data, and types of numerical and graphical summaries could be used to make sense of the data.
Interpret non-standard data visualizations from the media or scientific papers to make sense of real world phenomenon.

topics.name: Statistical inference
topics.description: Use informal and formal inference to make decisions in real contexts. Covers simulated sampling distributions, confidence intervals for proportions, and one-proportion z-tests.
topics.statement: Apply informal and formal statistical inference to make sense of, and make decisions in, meaningful real world contexts.

objectives.statement: Design a simulation to create a sampling distribution that can be used in making informal statistical inferences.
Construct confidence intervals of population proportions in the context of the data.
Implement a one proportion z-test to determine if an observed proportion is significantly different from a hypothesized proportion.

topics.name: Probability distributions
topics.description: Use probability distributions to make decisions under uncertainty. Covers discrete distributions and expected value, the binomial distribution, the normal approximation of sampling distributions, and normal probabilities.
topics.statement: Apply probability distributions in making decisions in uncertainty.

objectives.statement: Implement discrete probability distributions to model random phenomenon and make decisions (e.g., expected value of playing a game, etc.).
Implement the binomial distribution to model situations and make decisions.
Recognize from simulations of sampling distributions of sample means and proportions that a normal distribution can be used as an approximate model in certain situations.
Implement the normal distribution as a probability distribution to determine the likelihood of events occurring.

topics.name: Complex number operations
topics.description: Apply the properties of complex numbers and the complex number system. Covers adding, subtracting and multiplying complex numbers.
topics.statement: Apply properties of complex numbers and the complex number system.

objectives.statement: Execute the sum and difference algorithms to combine complex numbers.
Execute the multiplication algorithm with complex numbers.

topics.name: Matrix operations
topics.description: Apply the properties of matrix operations. Covers matrix addition and subtraction, associative, distributive and commutative properties, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.
topics.statement: Apply properties and operations with matrices.

objectives.statement: Execute the sum and difference algorithms to combine matrices of appropriate dimensions.
Execute associative and distributive properties to matrices.
Execute commutative property to add matrices.
Execute properties of matrices to multiply a matrix by a scalar.
Execute the multiplication algorithm with matrices.

topics.name: Vector operations
topics.description: Understand the properties of vectors and operate with them. Covers representing magnitude and direction, and adding and subtracting vectors.
topics.statement: Understand properties and operations with vectors.

objectives.statement: Represent a vector indicating magnitude and direction.
Execute sum and difference algorithms to combine vectors.

topics.name: Rational and polynomial inequalities
topics.description: Solve one-variable inequalities involving rational and polynomial expressions. Covers sign analysis and graphical methods.
topics.statement: Apply properties of solving inequalities that include rational and polynomial expressions in one variable.

objectives.statement: Implement algebraic (sign analysis) methods to solve rational and polynomial inequalities.
Implement graphical methods to solve rational and polynomial inequalities.

topics.name: Exponential, logarithmic and trig equations
topics.description: Solve equations involving exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions. Covers logarithm properties, exponential and logarithmic equations, trig equations with inverse functions and identities, and eliminating the parameter.
topics.statement: Apply properties of solving equations involving exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions.

objectives.statement: Use properties of logarithms to rewrite expressions.
Implement properties of exponentials and logarithms to solve equations.
Implement properties of trigonometric functions to solve equations including inverse trigonometric functions; double angle formulas, and Pythagorean identities.
Implement algebraic techniques to rewrite parametric equations in cartesian form by eliminating the parameter.

topics.name: Graphs of the six trig functions
topics.description: Understand the key features of all six trigonometric functions. Covers features of transformed sine and cosine, of tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant, building trig functions, and solving trig equations and inequalities.
topics.statement: Understand key features of sine, cosine, tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant functions.

objectives.statement: Interpret algebraic and graphical representations to determine key features of transformed sine and cosine functions. Key features include: amplitude, domain, midline, phase shift, frequency, period, intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive or negative, relative maximums and minimums.

Interpret algebraic and graphical representations to determine key features of tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant. Key features include: domain, frequency, period, intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive or negative, relative maximums and minimums, and asymptotes.
Integrate information to build trigonometric functions with specified amplitude, frequency, period, phase shift, or midline with or without context.
Implement graphical and algebraic methods to solve trigonometric equations and inequalities in context with support from technology.

topics.name: The unit circle
topics.description: Use the unit circle to find values of the six trigonometric functions. Covers reference angles, and how the circle's symmetry gives periodicity.
topics.statement: Apply properties of a unit circle with center (0,0) to determine the values of sine, cosine, tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant.

objectives.statement: Use a unit circle to find values of sine, cosine, and tangent for angles in terms of reference angles.
Explain the relationship between the symmetry of a unit circle and the periodicity of trigonometric functions

topics.name: Trigonometry of any triangle
topics.description: Use trigonometry to solve problems with any triangle. Covers all solutions of inverse trig equations, the Law of Sines and Law of Cosines, and the Pythagorean identity.
topics.statement: Apply properties of trigonometry to solve problems involving all types of triangles.

objectives.statement: Implement a strategy to generate all solutions to an equation that involves inverse trigonometric functions.
Implement the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to solve problems.
Implement the Pythagorean identity to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

topics.name: Exponential, log, rational functions, conics
topics.description: Relate algebraic and graphical forms of exponential, logarithmic, rational and power functions and conic sections to their key features. Covers key features, growth and decay models, equations, optimization, transformations, and identifying conics.
topics.statement: Understand the relationship of algebraic and graphical representations of exponential, logarithmic, rational, power functions, and conic sections to their key features.

objectives.statement: Interpret algebraic and graphical representations to determine key features of exponential functions. Key features include: domain, range, intercepts, intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive or negative, concavity, end behavior, limits, and asymptotes.
Integrate information to build exponential functions to model phenomena involving growth or decay.

Interpret algebraic and graphical representations to determine key features of logarithmic functions. Key features include: domain, range, intercepts, intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive or negative, concavity, end behavior, continuity, limits, and asymptotes.
Implement graphical and algebraic methods to solve exponential and logarithmic equations in context with support from technology.

Interpret algebraic and graphical representations to determine key features of rational functions. Key features include: domain, range, intercepts, intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive or negative, concavity, end behavior, continuity, limits, and asymptotes.
Implement graphical and algebraic methods to solve optimization problems given rational and polynomial functions in context with support from technology.
Construct graphs of transformations of power, exponential, and logarithmic functions showing key features.
Identify the conic section (ellipse, hyperbola, parabola) from its algebraic representation in standard form.

Interpret algebraic and graphical representations to determine key features of conic sections (ellipse: center, length of the major and minor axes; hyperbola: vertices, transverse axis; parabola: vertex, axis of symmetry)

topics.name: Composition and inverse functions
topics.description: Build new functions by composition. Covers composing and evaluating composites, domains of composites, composition models, decomposing functions, finding inverses, and checking inverses by composition.
topics.statement: Apply properties of function composition to build new functions from existing functions.

objectives.statement: Implement algebraic procedures to compose functions.
Execute a procedure to determine the value of a composite function at a given value using algebraic, graphical, and tabular representations.
Implement algebraic methods to find the domain of a composite function.
Organize information to build models involving function composition.
Deconstruct a composite function into two functions.
Implement algebraic and graphical methods to find an inverse function of an existing function, restricting domains if necessary.
Use composition to determine if one function is the inverse of another function.

topics.name: Recursive functions
topics.description: Build recursive functions to solve problems. Covers recursive functions from algebraic rules and from numerical sequences.
topics.statement: Apply mathematical reasoning to build recursive functions and solve problems.

objectives.statement: Use algebraic representations to build recursive functions.
Construct a recursive function for a sequence represented numerically.

topics.name: Parametric functions
topics.description: Build parametric functions to solve problems. Covers representing situations with parametric equations and solving contextual problems with technology.
topics.statement: Apply mathematical reasoning to build parametric functions and solve problems.

objectives.statement: Implement algebraic methods to represent a situation using parametric equations.
Implement technology to solve contextual problems involving parametric equations.
